04/09/2025, 21:13 - SANJAY M: Welcome to our project demonstration — Calculating Family Expenses using ServiceNow.

Managing household finances can often be overwhelming. Families deal with multiple categories of spending — from daily expenses to larger allocations for healthcare, education, or entertainment. Without the right system, it becomes hard to track where the money is going, spot overspending, or plan ahead. Our solution addresses this challenge by building a smart, structured expense management system on the ServiceNow platform.

Here’s how it works. Every family expense entry is recorded with key details such as the date, category, and amount. For example, in our demo database, we have a record with ID MFE0001005, dated 13th August 2025. In this case, 40,000 was allocated to overall family expenses, while 30,000 was specifically used for daily expenses. The platform doesn’t just store this information — it categorizes it instantly, compares it against pre-set budgets, and presents clear visual reports.

With ServiceNow’s reporting and dashboards, families can quickly see how much is being spent on essentials versus non-essentials, whether certain categories are crossing their limits, and what trends are developing over time. For example, the system might highlight that grocery expenses have steadily risen for the last three months, or that transport costs exceeded the monthly allowance. This insight allows families to adjust their spending habits before it becomes a problem.

The project also goes beyond simple tracking. By integrating with IoT devices, expenses like electricity usage or smart grocery purchases can be added automatically, making the system both accurate and efficient. With ServiceNow’s scalability, this solution works for small families as well as larger households, ensuring all financial data stays centralized and easy to access.

In short, our Family Expenses project empowers families to take control of their finances. It transforms raw numbers into meaningful insights, helping households make better decisions today, while also preparing them for a more financially secure future.

08/09/2025, 07:04 - SANJAY M: Compile Time Binding

If the compiler knows exactly where in memory the program will reside, it directly generates absolute addresses.

Once compiled, the program must always run from that same memory location
08/09/2025, 07:04 - SANJAY M: Load Time Binding

If memory location is not known at compile time, the compiler generates relocatable code.

Final binding is done by the loader, when the program is loaded into memory.

Program can be placed in different memory locations each time it runs, but cannot move after loading.
08/09/2025, 07:05 - SANJAY M: If a process can be moved during execution (swapping, virtual memory), binding must be delayed until run time.

Requires hardware support → Memory Management Unit (MMU).

Logical addresses (generated by CPU) are converted to physical addresses on the fly.

11/09/2025, 19:35 - Divya 🩶(LP): Welcome to our project demonstration — Calculating Family Expenses using ServiceNow.

Managing household finances can often be overwhelming. Families deal with multiple categories of spending — from daily expenses to larger allocations for healthcare, education, or entertainment. Without the right system, it becomes hard to track where the money is going, spot overspending, or plan ahead. Our solution addresses this challenge by building a smart, structured expense management system on the ServiceNow platform.

Here’s how it works. Every family expense entry is recorded with key details such as the date, category, and amount. For example, in our demo database, we have a record with ID MFE0001005, dated 13th August 2025. In this case, 40,000 was allocated to overall family expenses, while 30,000 was specifically used for daily expenses. The platform doesn’t just store this information — it categorizes it instantly, compares it against pre-set budgets, and presents clear visual reports.

With ServiceNow’s reporting and dashboards, families can quickly see how much is being spent on essentials versus non-essentials, whether certain categories are crossing their limits, and what trends are developing over time. For example, the system might highlight that grocery expenses have steadily risen for the last three months, or that transport costs exceeded the monthly allowance. This insight allows families to adjust their spending habits before it becomes a problem.

The project also goes beyond simple tracking. By integrating with IoT devices, expenses like electricity usage or smart grocery purchases can be added automatically, making the system both accurate and efficient. With ServiceNow’s scalability, this solution works for small families as well as larger households, ensuring all financial data stays centralized and easy to access.

In short, our Family Expenses project empowers families to take control of their finances. It transforms raw numbers into meaningful insights, helping households make better decisions today, while also preparing them for a more financially secure future.

Thank you.

26/10/2025, 17:23 - SANJAY M: Title Slide
Calculating Family Expenses using ServiceNow
Team ID: NM2025TMID20269
Team Leader: Sanjay M
Members: Kabilan M, Ranjith K, Israr Ahmed A
Category: ServiceNow System Administrator

Problem & Objective

Manual expense tracking leads to inefficiency and errors.

Difficult to analyze spending patterns; lacks financial visibility.

Need for a structured and automated system.

Objective: Build a ServiceNow-based expense calculation system for categorization, real-time tracking, reporting, and budgeting alerts.

Overview: Skills, System & Workflow
Skills Required:

IoT & Open Hardware Platforms

Data Structures

ServiceNow System Administration

System Overview:

Centralized dashboard on ServiceNow

Dynamic numbering, auto-calculated expense records

Generates analytical reports

Project Workflow:

Set up ServiceNow instance

Create Local Update Set

Design Database Tables

Configure Auto-Number & Business Rules

Establish Table Relationships

Final Configuration & Testing

Milestones 1–5: Setup & Core Table Design

Milestone 1: Developer account, ServiceNow instance setup

Milestone 2 & 3: "Family Expenses" update set creation & activation

Milestone 4: Build Family Expenses table (Number, Date, Amount, Details)

Milestone 5: Configure auto-number (MFE prefix), mandatory/read-only fields

Milestones 6–11: Linking & Daily Expenses Automation

Milestone 6–7: Build Daily Expenses table (Number, Date, Expense, Member, Comments), auto-number

Milestone 8–10: Link Daily Expenses to Family Expenses, modules, related lists

Milestone 11: Implement business rules for calculation, record sync

Milestones 12–15: Refinement, Outcomes & Impact

Milestones 12–14: Refine relationships with scripts, optimize fetching & sync

Milestone 15: Final system refinement & testing

Outcome: Automated expense management, real-time reports, improved budgeting

Conclusion
The ServiceNow system improves financial transparency, ease of tracking, and budgeting discipline with automation and real-time analytics.

Future Enhancement

Mobile app

AI-based insights

Group tracking

Bank integration

Multilingual support

Your questions and feedback are welcome!

14/11/2025, 09:12 - SANJAY M: User authentication and authorization are crucial aspects of security in software applications.

*Authentication:*
Verifying the identity of users, ensuring they are who they claim to be.

- Methods:
    - Username and password
    - Biometrics (fingerprint, facial recognition)
    - OTP (One-Time Password)
    - Social media login

*Authorization:*
Granting access to resources and functionality based on user identity and permissions.

- Methods:
    - Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
    - Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC)
    - Mandatory Access Control (MAC)

13/12/2025, 18:58 - Divya 🩶(LP): To save money, you need to you to save it by budgeting, cutting unnecessary spending (wants vs. needs), paying off high-interest debt first, and automating savings into a separate account, using strategies like the 50/30/20 rule and smart shopping to free up cash for your financial goals like emergencies or big purchases. 
1. Set Up Your System
Budget: Track income and expenses to see where money goes, distinguishing needs (rent, food) from wants (dining out, subscriptions).
Pay Yourself First: Set up automatic transfers to a dedicated savings account on payday, treating savings as a non-negotiable bill.
Automate: Use apps or bank features to automate savings and bill payments, reducing temptation. 
2. Reduce Spending
Needs vs. Wants: Learn to differentiate essentials from lifestyle extras.
Cut Subscriptions: Cancel unused memberships and streaming services.
Shop Smart: Compare prices, use coupons, buy second-hand (especially for kids' items), and avoid impulse buys by waiting a few days.
Lower Bills: Conserve energy (lights off, unplug devices) and shop around for better insurance/phone plans. 
3. Handle Debt & Build Security
Prioritize High-Interest Debt: Pay off credit cards and loans with high interest rates first, as this saves you more long-term.
Build an Emergency Fund: Save 3-6 months of living expenses in an easily accessible savings account for unexpected events. 
4. Grow Your Savings
Use Savings Accounts: Earn interest in basic savings or get higher rates with fixed deposits for money you won't need soon.
Invest: Once secure, invest money for long-term goals to make it grow faster. 
Popular Savings Rules:
50/30/20 Rule: 50% Needs, 30% Wants, 20% Savings.
70/30 Rule: Spend 70%, Save 20%, Give 10%.

28/12/2025, 10:24 - Divya 🩶(LP): Data science helps organisations turn raw data into useful knowledge, decisions, and intelligent products.


1. Roles of data science
Decision support and strategy: Data science converts data into insights that guide pricing, marketing, risk, and operations decisions (for example, which customers to target, which products to stock).


Descriptive, predictive, prescriptive analytics: It explains what happened (reports, dashboards), predicts what will happen (churn, demand), and recommends what action to take (best offer, optimal route).


Automation and AI products: It powers features like recommendation systems, fraud‑detection engines, chatbots, and predictive maintenance so that software can act automatically instead of only reporting.


Business optimisation: By analysing processes, data science finds bottlenecks and reduces cost, for example optimising delivery routes or scheduling machines to reduce downtime.


2. Stages of data science (with examples)
A typical data‑science lifecycle can be written in assignment form as below.


Problem definition / business understanding

Clarify the question and success metrics.


Example: An e‑commerce site wants to reduce customer churn by 10% in the next quarter.


Data collection and understanding

Gather data from databases, logs, sensors, or external APIs and study its structure and quality.


Example: Collect past orders, website click logs, and customer service tickets for all users from the last 2 years.


Data cleaning and preparation (feature engineering)

Handle missing values, remove duplicates, fix formats, create useful features, and split data into training and test sets.


Example: Create a feature “days since last purchase” or “average order value” for each customer and remove obviously wrong records.


Exploratory data analysis (EDA)

Use statistics and visualisation to find patterns, correlations, and outliers.


Example: Plot churn rate vs. number of support complaints to see if unhappy customers are leaving.


Model building and evaluation

Choose algorithms (logistic regression, decision trees, random forest, neural networks), train models, and evaluate them using metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, RMSE, etc.


Example: Build a churn‑prediction model and evaluate it on a test set; if recall for “will churn” is low, tune hyperparameters or try another algorithm.


Deployment and monitoring

Integrate the model into production systems (web app, API, dashboard) and track performance over time; retrain when data changes.


Example: Show a real‑time “churn risk score” on the CRM screen so support staff can offer discounts; regularly monitor if model accuracy drops.


3. Applications and fields using data science
Major application areas
Healthcare: Disease prediction, medical image analysis (X‑ray, MRI), drug discovery, hospital resource optimisation, personalised treatment plans.


Finance and banking: Fraud detection, credit‑risk scoring, algorithmic trading, customer segmentation, and personalised financial advice.


Retail and e‑commerce: Recommendation systems (“people also bought”), dynamic pricing, demand forecasting, inventory optimisation, and targeted marketing.


Transportation and logistics: Route optimisation for delivery vehicles, ride‑sharing matching (e.g., assigning drivers), traffic prediction, and fleet maintenance.


Manufacturing and IoT: Predictive maintenance using sensor data, quality inspection using image recognition, and optimisation of production lines.


Social media and digital platforms: News‑feed ranking, ad targeting, spam detection, sentiment analysis of posts and comments.


Example fields / domains
You can list these as bullet points in your assignment:

Healthcare, pharmaceuticals, and biotechnology.


Banking, insurance, fintech, and stock markets.


Retail, e‑commerce, and marketing analytics.


Transport, logistics, ride‑sharing, and supply‑chain management.


Manufacturing, energy, smart factories, and predictive maintenance.


Government, smart cities, public safety, and policy planning.


If you say what word limit your teacher wants (for example “one page each answer”), a ready‑to‑submit paragraph version can be shaped from this outline.

24/02/2026, 10:55 - Divya 🩶(LP): 1. Amazon Web Services (AWS)
Amazon Web Services is the largest and most widely used cloud computing platform in the world. It provides more than 200 fully featured services.
Key Services:
EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud): Virtual servers for running applications.
S3 (Simple Storage Service): Object storage for storing files and images.
RDS (Relational Database Service): Managed database service.
Lambda: Serverless computing.
Features:
Highly scalable infrastructure.
Pay-as-you-go pricing model.
Global data centers.
Strong security and compliance support.
Advantages:
Large community and documentation.
Supports AI, IoT, big data, and analytics.
Highly reliable and flexible.
Disadvantages:
Complex pricing structure.
Can be difficult for beginners.
2. Google Compute Engine (GCE)
Google Compute Engine is part of Google Cloud Platform. It provides high-performance virtual machines running in Google’s data centers.
Key Services:
Compute Engine: Virtual machines.
Cloud Storage: File storage.
Cloud SQL: Managed database.
AI and Machine Learning Tools: TensorFlow integration.
Features:
Fast and high-performance network.
Strong support for AI and machine learning.
Simple and transparent pricing.
Integrated with Google services.
Advantages:
Best for AI and data analytics projects.
Clean user interface.
Cost-effective for startups.
Disadvantages:
Smaller market share than AWS.
Fewer services compared to AWS.
3. Microsoft Azure Virtual Machine
Microsoft Azure is a cloud computing service developed by Microsoft. Azure Virtual Machines allow users to deploy and manage applications in the cloud.
Key Services:
Azure Virtual Machines: Scalable virtual servers.
Azure Blob Storage: File and image storage.
Azure SQL Database: Managed relational database.
Azure App Service: Web app hosting.
Features:
Strong integration with Microsoft products.
Enterprise-level security.
Hybrid cloud support.
Scalable infrastructure.
Advantages:
Best for Windows-based applications.
Good enterprise support.
Easy integration with .NET and Microsoft tools.
Disadvantages:
Can be expensive for small projects.
Complex management for beginners
24/02/2026, 10:55 - Divya 🩶(LP): Conclusion
AWS, Google Compute Engine, and Microsoft Azure are leading cloud platforms that provide virtual machines and cloud infrastructure services. AWS offers the largest number of services and global presence. Google Compute Engine is best suited for AI and machine learning workloads. Microsoft Azure is ideal for enterprise and Windows-based environments.
The choice of platform depends on project requirements, budget, scalability needs, and technical expertise.

– Briefly explain your background, education, and skills.

– Show that you know about the company and are interested.

– Example: Hardworking, quick learner, good communication.

– Mention a small weakness and say how you are improving it.

– Explain what skills and value you can bring to the company.

– Talk about career growth and learning.

– Share a real situation and solution.

– Give a positive reason (learning, growth, new opportunity).

– Show that you researched the company.

– Example: Ask about training, growth, or team culture.

16/03/2026, 10:45 - Divya 🩶(LP): Here are simple sample answers you can use in an interview:
1️⃣ Tell me about yourself
“My name is Divya Bharathi. I completed my education and I am very interested in starting my career in a good company. I am a hardworking person, a quick learner, and I like to improve my communication skills. I enjoy learning new things and working with a team.”
2️⃣ Why do you want to work for this company?
“I want to work for this company because it has a good reputation and provides opportunities to learn and grow. I believe this company will help me improve my skills and build my career.”
3️⃣ What are your strengths?
“My strengths are that I am hardworking, a quick learner, and a positive thinker. I also have good communication skills and I can work well in a team.”
4️⃣ What are your weaknesses?
“One of my weaknesses is that sometimes I take extra time to make sure my work is perfect. But I am learning to manage my time better and work more efficiently.”
5️⃣ Why should we hire you?
“You should hire me because I am dedicated, eager to learn, and ready to work hard. I will give my best to help the company grow and provide good service.”
6️⃣ Where do you see yourself in 5 years?
“In five years, I see myself in a responsible position in the company where I can use my skills and experience to contribute more to the organization.”
7️⃣ Tell me about a challenge you faced and how you solved it
“During my studies, I once had difficulty completing a project on time. I managed my time better, asked for guidance, and worked hard to complete it successfully.”
8️⃣ Why did you leave your last job?
“I am looking for better opportunities to learn new skills and grow in my career.”
9️⃣ What do you know about our company?
“I know that your company has a good reputation and focuses on providing quality service to customers. It is also known for supporting employee growth.”
🔟 Do you have any questions for us?
“Yes, I would like to know about the training process and growth opportunities in this company.”

25/03/2026, 22:57 - Divya 🩶(LP): ## CHAPTER 5: TESTING AND DEPLOYMENT

### 5.1 Software Testing Methodologies
A multi-layered testing strategy was employed to ensure the stability and security of the platform before final deployment.

#### 1. Unit Testing
Individual modules, particularly the **AI Bridge (Python)** and **Auth Middleware (Node.js)**, were tested independently to ensure they handle edge cases (e.g., invalid API keys or expired JWT tokens).

#### 2. Integration Testing
Verified the communication between the Glassmorphism frontend and the Express backend. This ensured that the `FormData` sent from the camera module was correctly parsed and stored as a Buffer in the database.

#### 3. User Acceptance Testing (UAT)
Conducted with a small group of mock "donors" and "NGO staff" to verify that the UI was intuitive and that the "One-Click Claim" process was functional.

### 5.2 Test Case Table

| Test ID | feature | Input | Expected Result | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| TC-01 | User Registration | Valid details & unique username | Data saved in `Users` collection | **PASS** |
| TC-02 | AI Food Scan | Photo of a "Vegetable Curry" | JSON identifying item and portions | **PASS** |
| TC-03 | Atomic Claiming | Two NGOs claim same item simultaneously | Only one succeeds; other gets error | **PASS** |
| TC-04 | Point Redemption | Request item with insufficient points | System displays "Not enough points" | **PASS** |
| TC-05 | Admin Payout | Uploading payment screenshot | Status updates to "Completed" for user | **PASS** |

### 5.3 Deployment Workflow
The system is designed for modern cloud infrastructure:
- **Backend/API:** Deployed using **Vercel** or **Heroku** with environment variables for Gemini API Keys.
- **Database:** Hosted on **MongoDB Atlas** for high-availability production clusters.
- **Frontend Assets:** Optimized through CDN delivery to ensure fast loading of glassmorphism CSS.

---

## CHAPTER 6: CONCLUSION AND FUTURE ENHANCEMENTS

### 6.1 Conclusion
The **Food Reduction Management** system successfully demonstrates how modern AI can be applied to solve the critical social problem of food waste. By bridging the gap between donors and receivers through a transparent, gamified, and AI-powered platform, the project provides a scalable template for smart urban sustainability. The platform reduces the technical barrier for hotels to donate food while ensuring that orphanages receive high-quality nutrition in real-time.

### 6.2 Socio-Economic Impact
- **Waste Reduction:** Drastically lowers the carbon footprint associated with landfilling perishable food.
- **Social Support:** Strengthens the resource pool for charitable institutions that lack consistent funding.
- **Corporate Social Responsibility:** Provides businesses with an auditable and rewarding way to contribute to the community.

### 6.3 Future Enhancements
- **Geolocation Integration:** Implementing Google Maps API for optimized pickup routes and real-time navigation for NGOs.
- **Push Notifications:** Alerting nearby orphanages immediately when a high-priority/large donation is posted.
- **Predictive Analytics:** Using historical data trends to help hotels forecast food waste and adjust their future procurement strategies using AI.
- **Blockchain for Transparency:** Implementing a distributed ledger for donation logs to ensure immutable records of social impact.
